candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record and histopathology strongly support lichen planus, specifically affecting the nails. However, the reference diagnosis specifies 'bullous' and 'of the nails', which are not fully captured by the general 'Lichen planus' candidate.

The clinical presentation (painful swelling, violaceous discoloration, nail dystrophy, oral lichenoid plaques) and histopathology (hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, basal cell degeneration, apoptotic keratinocytes, dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate) are highly characteristic of lichen planus. There is no evidence in the record to suggest paraneoplastic pemphigus, which typically involves severe mucocutaneous blistering and specific autoantibodies not mentioned here.
